status: draft — scholar review required for every 'why' and grade
rule: Show a virtue only with a sahih or hasan source. If narrations are weak, say so plainly and show none.

passages.title: Āyat al-Kursī
passages.why: Called the greatest āyah in the Book of Allah.

passages.title: Last two āyāt of Al-Baqarah
passages.why: Whoever recites them at night, they will suffice him.

passages.title: Al-Mulk
passages.why: A surah of thirty āyāt that interceded for a man until he was forgiven.

passages.title: As-Sajdah
passages.why: The Prophet ﷺ would not sleep until he recited Alif-Lām-Mīm Tanzīl (As-Sajdah) and Tabārak (Al-Mulk).

passages.title: Al-Kahf · first ten āyāt
passages.why: Whoever memorises the first ten āyāt of Al-Kahf is protected from the Dajjāl.

passages.title: Al-Kahf
passages.why: Commonly recited on Fridays; narrations in al-Ḥākim and al-Bayhaqī are graded authentic by some scholars.

passages.title: Āl ʿImrān · last eleven āyāt
passages.why: The Prophet ﷺ recited them on waking for the night prayer.

passages.title: Yā-Sīn
passages.why: Widely loved and recited. Narrations about specific virtues of this surah are weak, so the app does not show them.

passages.title: Ar-Raḥmān
passages.why: A favourite for its refrain “Which of your Lord’s favours will you deny?” No virtue narration is shown.

passages.title: Al-Wāqiʿah
passages.why: Widely recited. Narrations about its virtue are weak, so none is shown.

passages.title: Al-Ḥashr · last three āyāt
passages.why: Some of the most beautiful names of Allah in one passage. No virtue narration is shown.

passages.title: Friday Fajr: As-Sajdah and Al-Insān
passages.why: The Prophet ﷺ recited them in Fajr on Fridays.

passages.title: Jumuʿah: Al-Aʿlā & Al-Ghāshiyah, or Al-Jumuʿah & Al-Munāfiqūn
passages.why: Both pairs were recited by the Prophet ﷺ in the Jumuʿah prayer.

passages.title: Eid: Al-Aʿlā & Al-Ghāshiyah, or Qāf & Al-Qamar
passages.why: Recited by the Prophet ﷺ in the Eid prayers.

passages.title: Witr: Al-Aʿlā, Al-Kāfirūn, Al-Ikhlāṣ
passages.why: Recited by the Prophet ﷺ in the three rakʿāt of witr.
